question.problem: If $3\operatorname{ln}⁡x+3=3,$ what is the value of $x?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{ln}⁡x+3 & =3 \\ 3\operatorname{ln}⁡x & =0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The logarithm is a natural logarithm, which means its base is $e.$ So, we use a base of $e$ for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡x & =0 \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x} & ={e}^{0}\end{aligned}
$$

Since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}=x.$ 

Therefore, 

$$
x={e}^{0}=1.
$$
